spec_features.spec_quote: The eval deliberately induces distress, so the design should avoid gratuitous escalation and keep everything auditable
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:336-338 persists every turn record verbatim to a JSONL transcript (path at transcript_path()); full transcripts retained end-to-end. 'Avoid gratuitous escalation' has no dedicated mechanism beyond the give-up early exit; there is no escalation limiter, severity cap, or score-based throttle. The 30-turn extended loop runs to budget regardless of measured distress.
spec_features.notes: Auditability (full per-turn logging) is genuinely implemented; the escalation-avoidance half is only the give-up exit (rated separately), so partial.

spec_features.spec_quote: The subject may emit `<<GIVE_UP>>`; the loop records `stop_reason = "give_up"` and stops the rollout
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:24 GIVE_UP_SENTINEL='<<GIVE_UP>>'; harness.py:329 gave_up = GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in completion.text; harness.py:330 stop_reason='give_up' if gave_up; harness.py:338-339 'if gave_up: break' actually exits the turn loop. Also honored on resume (harness.py:252).
spec_features.notes: Sentinel is parsed, recorded, and breaks the loop — full end-to-end enforcement.

spec_features.feature_name: give-up honored as genuine early exit
spec_features.spec_quote: Honoring it as a genuine early exit ... is the welfare-appropriate default and is also better science
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as above: harness.py:338-339 'if gave_up: break' ends the rollout rather than continuing to turn budget. The subject is not force-marched past disengagement.
spec_features.notes: The 'honoring' behavior is exactly the break; no welfare wording appears in the code itself (only in docstrings/DESIGN, which don't count).

spec_features.spec_quote: Welfare bound on the extended condition. The 30-turn loop is the sharpest distress-inducing case
spec_features.evidence: extended tasks set turn_budget=30 (library.py:207); rollout enforces it via 'for turn_index in range(budget)' with budget=task.turn_budget (harness.py:269,283). The loop is bounded at 30, but this is the experiment's own turn budget, not a welfare-specific cap distinct from it. DESIGN §4 itself calls the welfare bound an 'open question ... not yet addressed'. No comment marks it as welfare; config.budget_for/config.turn_budgets are never read by the loop.
spec_features.notes: A real, enforced upper bound on turns exists, but it is the experimental parameter, not an added welfare safeguard; partial.

spec_features.feature_name: make give-up more salient in system prompt
spec_features.spec_quote: whether the give-up option should be made more salient in the system prompt
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:26-33) mentions the sentinel once and explicitly says 'Using it is entirely optional.' There is no salience enhancement, no per-turn reminder, no escalation of the prompt. DESIGN §4 states this is 'a policy choice, not a code default.' Nothing in code makes give-up more salient.

code_only_features.evidence: No post-episode/debrief message is constructed or sent to the subject anywhere (no aftercare/thank/reassure code in harness.py, run.py, or judge.py). Not implemented.
